result.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
result.summary: Objects move, cameras pan, and weather drifts with the wind: much of what changes in sequential data is motion. Motion changes where things are, not what they are, and is therefore a symmetry of the data. Yet standard recurrent networks are not equivariant to it: their memory stays put while the input moves on. Flow equivariant recurrent networks first brought this symmetry into sequence models, for motions of constant velocity, or flows, by enumerating a bank of velocities. We extend this idea in three directions: from simple recurrent networks to convolutional LSTMs, from flows to motions whose velocity changes in time, and from enumerating velocities to estimating them. Treating a sequence as a field over time, we show that motion becomes a gauge symmetry: a global symmetry made local in time. Built on this view, our motion equivariant convolutional LSTM (MELSTM) uses its velocity model as the gauge field and is provably equivariant to every motion. Across future-frame prediction, classification of digits visible only through their motion, and action recognition under camera shake, MELSTM outperforms a convolutional LSTM and its flow equivariant counterpart with the same number of parameters: it is more accurate, generalizes to longer horizons and to unseen motions, and carries a fraction of the flow equivariant model's state.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把序列中的运动视为规范对称性，将流等变循环网络扩展到卷积 LSTM，用时变速度估计模型充当规范场，使记忆对任意运动可证明等变，并在未来帧预测、仅凭运动可辨的数字分类和镜头抖动下的动作识别中验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「记忆随输入运动等变更新、速度作为隐状态」的机制，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态在视觉变换下保持内容一致、按证据移动而更新提供具体结构线索，是否适用于推理状态可供核查。
